about.beginner: SovRing-Labs is one person's open research lab building AI that runs on the computers people already own. Its core idea is the residue ring: numbers and memories stored as remainders on several small prime 'rings', which makes some arithmetic exact and order-independent and lets a memory be found by its address instead of by searching. The repositories are the engines (exact ring arithmetic, ring memory, a shared-memory vector core), the agent tooling that runs a fleet of AI coding agents safely and cheaply, a from-scratch web browser engine, and the research papers with the scripts that produced every number. Each repository has a quick test you can run in minutes, and each claim it makes has a test you can re-run.
about.intermediate: Engines: armilla-astrolabe (carry-free residue-number-system arithmetic on CPUs: exact sums, sign/ReLU from the rings, an exact training step), omni-ring (vector-symbolic / hyperdimensional memory on rings with an AVX2 C kernel), vsa-core (shared-memory hypervector bus in C). Agents: talon (agent engine), tarsus (safety and tool-call repair), dock (one MCP front for many MCP servers), cost-savers (token reduction), agent-reliability-kit (routing, grounding, a done-gate), omnid (local embeddings and an MCP face). Browser: omni-render (rendering engine with integer layout and a JS runtime) and omni-ui (apps and a light browser on it). Research: omniring-research (the measured corpus, CC BY 4.0, with its harness). Licences: the engines and agent tools are PolyForm Small Business OR Noncommercial (free trial for evaluation); dock and omnid are Apache-2.0; the browser is MIT OR Apache-2.0; the corpus is CC BY 4.0.
about.advanced: Every repository carries DOSSIER.md (history, metrics, limits), PROVENANCE.md (sources, clean-room notes), TECHNICAL-DISCLOSURE.md where it discloses a method as dated prior art, and CITATION.cff with a Zenodo DOI. Claims are tied to evidence files committed in the repo; suite.json lists each claim with its verify command, the expected output, what passing means, how the number was obtained and its honest limits. Corrections are logged and applied as errata in the research corpus. Start from llms.txt for raw links to all of these.

repos.limits: A cue is mandatory for resonance; unguided decoding is seed-dependent and abstains when it fails. Resonant capacity ≈ 12 marks per slot at one cue (the exhaustive sift reads more). repos.one_line: Packed ternary weights (P2 4 trits/byte, P3 1.6 bits/weight, L5 compute on storage) with integer-only kernels that are bit-identical on scalar, AVX2, AVX-512 and NEON, in C++ and Rust.
repos.summary: Status: under development — pre-alpha (`STATUS.md`). Defensive publication: `TECHNICAL-DISCLOSURE.md` (dated 2026-10-16; the DOI is minted by Zenodo on the first GitHub release). A ternary weight is −1, 0 or +1. This library stores such weights compactly and multiplies them against int8 activations with integer arithmetic only, so every back-end (portable C, AVX2, AVX-512, NEON) gives the same integers, bit for bit. It is the weight format our ternary models and the omnid inference daemon use.
repos.limits: The Rust AVX2 path did not compile before 2026-10-16 (93 missing-name and 12 unsafe-call errors with `-C target-cpu=native`), so `p2_avx2_exact` had never run; the portable build compiles it out. repos.one_line: A liquid ternary reservoir (N=1024, K=16, ternary recurrent weights, trained ridge readout) in plain-integer form and in ring-state form: state as residues on 15 rings with a 2-of-3 vote per tick, readout plate as 12-bit integers on 12 rings; compiled AVX2 kernel, exactness, fault and identity harnesses, and the negative results.
repos.summary: Status: under development — pre-alpha (`STATUS.md`). Defensive publication: `TECHNICAL-DISCLOSURE.md` (dated 2026-10-16; the DOI is minted by Zenodo on the first GitHub release). A liquid ternary reservoir is a small recurrent network that is never trained: 1,024 neurons, each reading 16 others through fixed random weights that are only −1 or +1, with a leak and a hard clip, all in integers. Only a linear readout on top is fitted (closed-form ridge regression). It turns a text, as a stream of token ids, into a vector.
repos.limits: The ring kernel is slower than plain integers.** Same mesh, bitwise-equal outputs: ring kernel 59–65 M neuron updates/s, scalar plain-integer C 41–48, batch-vectorised plain-integer AVX2 C 366–600 (2026-10-16, three repeats, laptop under desktop load). The 2026-10-14 run had 43–51 / 32–35 / 193–236, so the ring kernel is about 1.3× a scalar loop and **4–10× slower than the best plain-integer kernel**. An earlier status line said "about plain integers, not faster"; that compared against the NumPy twin and is withdrawn. The value of the ring form is exactness, fault repair, growth and …
